introduction: In 1863 the Ottoman government, pressed by Persia, ordered Bahá’u’lláh from Baghdad to Constantinople. He spent twelve days in a garden outside the city, where He declared His mission, and then travelled nearly four months overland and by sea with His family and companions. These readings are His verses of farewell, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s memories of the caravan, and reflections on what the exile achieved: each banishment, meant to end the Cause, carried it further. The Bible’s exiles and travellers keep company with them, Abraham leaving his country, the captives by the rivers of Babylon, Paul’s journeys “in hunger and thirst” and his protest at Philippi, the church “scattered abroad” that “went every where preaching”; Paul’s own verdict, that his imprisonment had “fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel”, is the guide’s conclusion. Dante speaks for the bitterness of banishment, and Jeremiah for what exiles owe the place they are sent.
questions: The exiles arrived “filled with joy and gladness”. What made that possible?
Readings 43 to 47 argue that each exile spread the Faith. Is that a reason to think persecution always fails? What would Gamaliel say?
‘Abdu’l-Bahá remembered how the caravan divided its work. What do such practical memories add to the sacred history?
Reading 5 is a formal protest. How does protest sit beside the acceptance of suffering found elsewhere in the guide?

outside.why: The Persian government asked that He be moved further off. Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, unto a land that I will shew thee.
A rose recalls the season of their arrival. The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come.
Exiles who arrived full of joy and at peace. At midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
Grandeur and power in exile, despite Shah and Sultan. Be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods.
“In the name of God and humanity we protest.” Paul at Philippi: they have beaten us openly uncondemned, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily.
“As long as Bahá’u’lláh is in Persia the country will not be at peace.” These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also.
An ambassador who worked for their destruction. Haman to the king: it is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.
When the friends heard the order of exile their hearts were torn. They all wept sore, sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more.
Twelve days of feast in the garden, under sentence of exile. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies.
He left as an exile, and with unheard-of honour. Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.
“The Spirit will depart from the region of Iraq.” It is expedient for you that I go away.
The Bird of Immortality has taken flight. Oh that I had wings like a dove! for then would I fly away.
The breezes of separation on the shores of Iraq. By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.
Verses of separation. Dante on his own banishment: thou shalt abandon everything beloved most tenderly; thou shalt have proof how savoureth of salt the bread of others.
A large party, and the duties divided. Jethro to Moses on the march: thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.
The work shared among the travellers. Look ye out among you seven men of honest report, whom we may appoint over this business.
Sixty stages in a time of famine. In journeyings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
Riding by night, they were told to keep awake. What I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.
A dervish begged to join, warned that the journey would be hard. Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
They reached the sea and heard its murmuring. They that go down to the sea in ships, these see the works of the Lord, and his wonders in the deep.
Arrival at the house the government assigned. They confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
In the capital He declined to pay court to ministers. Before Pilate he answered him to never a word. What is asserted by a prisoner’s refusal to plead?
It was thought the cause would be lost in Baghdad, and it spread. They that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word.
Had He not been sent to Baghdad the Cause would not have grown in Persia. The more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew.
Each banishment raised the banner in a new land. The things which happened unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel.
They thought exile would put out the Lamp. If it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it.

The departure and the voyage. Jeremiah to an exiled people: seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives. What did these exiles bring to the cities they were sent to?

shortfall: Readings 14 to 25 are a dozen short verses on the departure from Iraq in one image (the Bird has flown), and 26 to 34 are travellers’ recollections; each group shares a few companions.
